chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Abdillah Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Ayyub ibn Abd al-Rahman and Zayd ibn al-Hasan Abu al-Hasan and 'Abbād, all from Sa'd al-Iskaf, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is pleased to live my life and die my death and enter the Garden of Eden, let him hold fast to the branch that my Lord planted with His own hand; let him follow 'Ali and the successors after him and submit to their virtues, for they are the guided ones with whom Allah is pleased. Allah has given them my understanding and my knowledge, and they are my progeny from my flesh and my blood. I complain to Allah about their enemies from among my nation, those who deny their virtues and cut off my tie to them. By Allah, they will kill my son, and may Allah exclude them from my intercession.'

key_terms.الْهُدَاةُ الْمَرْضِيُّونَ: The guided ones with whom Allah is pleased

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of following 'Ali and the Imams for entering Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the theological link between the Prophet’s lineage and the Imams, identifying them as the 'branch' (Qadib) planted by God’s own hand, a metaphor for their divine selection and intrinsic purity. It underscores the Shia doctrine of *Wilayah* by warning that denial of the Imams' virtues leads to exclusion from the Prophet's intercession, specifically foretelling the martyrdom of Husayn (a.s.) as a pivotal event for the community. The chain of narration highlights the transmission of this core belief through early Shia scholars, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt as the sole source of true guidance.
